title: Rochdale man jailed for life for murdering wife Keeley Aspinall
excerpt: Kyle Howard, of Tweedale Street, Rochdale, must serve at least 21 years and six months for murdering Keeley Aspinall, 44, whose body he hid under a bed.
body:
A Rochdale man who stabbed his wife and hid her body under a bed has been jailed for life for her murder.

Kyle Howard, of Tweedale Street, was sentenced at Manchester Crown Court on Wednesday 18 November to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 21 years and six months for the murder of Keeley Aspinall, 44.

He had pleaded guilty on Monday 16 November, having previously denied the offence, Greater Manchester Police said.

According to police, Howard contacted them on 25 May and told call handlers he had killed his wife two days earlier. He said her body was beginning to smell.

Officers went to the couple's home on Tweedale Street, where Howard directed them to the bedroom, saying: "She's in there. She's underneath the bed." Ms Aspinall was found dead under the bed.

A Home Office post-mortem examination found she had a stab wound to the chest, bruising to her neck consistent with strangulation, and other scratches and bruises, the force said.

Police said Howard told officers the pair had been drinking and began arguing in the kitchen while Ms Aspinall was cooking. He admitted putting his hands around her neck and punching her, but said he could not remember exactly how the knife ended up in her chest.

While being booked into custody he made several confessions, including "I'm not denying it" and "I'll admit it, I'm not bothered", according to police.

GMP said its Major Incident Team uncovered a pattern of domestic abuse by Howard towards Ms Aspinall during the investigation.

In victim impact statements read in court, Ms Aspinall's mother said: "She was bright, talented, funny, caring and full of confidence. She was an excellent dancer, a skilled hairdresser and someone who loved her family deeply."

Her sister said: "I just wish I could have one more second with my sister, I miss her so much and I'll never get to see her again, that was his choice to take her away."

Detective Inspector Neil Higginson, the senior investigating officer, said: "Keeley was killed by the man who was supposed to love her, support her and keep her safe. Instead, Howard subjected her to the ultimate act of violence, taking her life in her own home before concealing her body and leaving her there for days."

He added: "This was a devastating act of domestic abuse which has robbed a family of a daughter, a relative and a loved one."

After his arrest in May, Howard spent several days in hospital being treated for an infection to his hand. He was discharged back into police custody on 1 June and charged with murder on 2 June.

Anyone affected by domestic abuse can report it to Greater Manchester Police on 101, online or through the force's Live Chat service, and should call 999 in an emergency. The Greater Manchester domestic abuse helpline is open Monday to Friday from 10am to 4pm, and End the Fear lists local support across Greater Manchester.

Source: Greater Manchester Police press office, press releases issued on 16 and 18 November 2026. Photograph: Rochdale Daily.
